title: What Actually Happens When You Get Hiccups?
sources: Scientific American, 'What causes hiccups?': a hiccup is a sudden involuntary contraction of the diaphragm followed by closure of the glottis, which makes the 'hic' sound; the reflex runs through the brainstem

Straus, Vasilakos, Wilson et al. 2003, BioEssays 25(6), 'A phylogenetic hypothesis for the origin of hiccough': hiccups may be a remnant of gill ventilation in tadpoles, which close the glottis so water does not enter the lungs (a hypothesis, not proven)
Guinness World Records / Smithsonian: Charles Osborne of Anthon, Iowa hiccuped continuously for 68 years (1922-1990), an estimated 430 million hiccups

lines.text: What actually happens when you get hiccups?
Something sets off a reflex deep in your brainstem,

lines.text: and your diaphragm, the big muscle under your lungs, suddenly jerks down.
